newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian PM accepts finance minister resignation.
newsitem.headline: Latvian PM accepts finance minister resignation.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele on Wednesday accepted the resignation of Finance Minister Aivar Kreituss after he was dismissed from his own political party, a government spokesman said.
"He (Shkele) accepted the letter of resignation and handed him a note of thanks for his work," the spokesman told Reuters.
Shkele will temporarily assume the post of finance minister and take the 1997 budget, which has been drawn up without a budget deficit, through parliament.
Kreituss was forced to quit because a minister who is not a member of a party cannot be in the government.

Kreituss was dismissed from the Democratic Party Samnieks, the largest party in the six-party government, amid rivalries with the leadership and accusations he was failing to fulfill the party's programme.
Kreituss said his job was actually to fulfill the government's programme. The government spokesman said Shkele would wait for the DPS to name candidates for the finance job.
Shkele also wanted to get rid of two finance ministry state minister posts and is talking with government parties on this.
The first reading of the budget is on Monday, and the important parliament budget and finance committee has recommended it should be passed at the first reading.
The government spokesman said Kreituss' resignation has not caused problems for the administration and that Shkele was working normally.
The deficit-free 1997 budget is one of Shkele's key economic policies and is part of the promises made to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in return for new credits.
The deficit last year soared to 90 million lats after a bank crisis and is this year expected to be 40 million lats.
